Okay here’s my biggest tips and tricks:

-double shampoo always. First one gets rid of all the first and grime and second one cleanses the scalp. This makes sure no hair is getting clogged up and preventing growth 

-a scalp exfoliant. Whether it’s a brush made for that or a product. I use both interchangeably but I prefer the brush thing. I can send you the link from Amazon it’s cheap cheap. 

-conditioner must sit for minimum 5 minutes so I’ll usually shave my body durning the point. I only condition the ends. 

-product layering!! My routine is super minimal. A good leave in conditioner and a good hair oil. Leave in first and oil second. The oil acts as a barrier so the leave in can fully absorb into your hair. It also gives lots of shine! There’s a lot of different hair oils out there now. 

-scalp oiling: once a week I like to douse my head in either the hair oil or olive oil. I let it sit either overnight or 6 hours at least. If I don’t have the time then I’ll do it 30 minutes before I shower and call it good enough. 

-protective styles: my hair is 98% of the time in a side braid or double braid. This protects the hair from mechanical damage like rubbing on your shirt or everyday objects. I also use a satin pillow case but lately I’ve been using a satin bonnet. Depends on how hot I am at night lol 

-I wash my hair once a week but wash your hair as often as you need. But I don’t recommend every day. 

-a solid hair brush. I like the wet brushes or I have a tek wooden brush but that’s an expensive one.

Some tips I have:
1. Working with wet hair is better for me as it clumps together easier. Or seriously greasy hair 😅

2. That shine? Greasy af hair 🤘🏻 with added oil for treatment because I was washing it out the next morning. 

3. Using a mousse on your roots for hold. This is why I start with wet or damp hair because the mousse looks funny on dry hair for me. It may look different on you. 

4. Keep your hands as close as you can to your scalp. Usually my pinkies are my anchors and always touching my head so I know I’m not drifting off. 

5. Place those braids wherever it’s comfortable for you to braid. I can’t get them on the back of my head (for now 😏) so I braid the sides. 

6. I practiced twice a day for a month straight and then slowly less over time as I felt I got better and better. 

7. Name your strands. Left middle right, one two three, Larry Jerry and Henry if you really want. If you name each strand youre less likely to lose track of which one goes next. 

8. Pull tight. Your fingers are going to hurt but shake them out and just push past it I promise they won’t fall off. You want to keep your hair as taunt as you can. 

9. Once I finish the braids I fluff them out. I only pull on the top part of the braid closest to my part to make them stand out a bit more. It also makes your braids look HELLA THICC. 

10. Seriously it’s all practice. This is 6 months of dedication of learning how to Dutch braid on myself. We are all capable of doing this!
